out.rationale: McAleese et al. note human-inserted bugs differ from natural LLM errors and suggest training models to insert subtle in-distribution problems. Kirchner et al. report sneaky-prover solutions become harder for time-limited humans to label correctly over rounds and suggest the sneaky prover could serve as a tampering model for training critique models; this comes from a pilot study with design flaws, on math rather than code.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether a trained model can generate subtle flaws for training critics instead of humans inserting bugs, for sneaky provers on grade-school math

text: When sneaky-prover solutions were shown to time-constrained contractors, the paper reports that the fraction labelled correctly was comparatively high but decreased over rounds, suggesting the sneaky prover could serve as a tampering model for training critique models; the authors note this result comes from a pilot study with design flaws.
title: Sneaky prover flaws get harder for time-limited humans to spot over rounds (pilot study)
